claims.text: Machine-learning optimization of sintering parameters can reduce the temperature needed for effective densification.
Heating rate, pressure, dwell time, and applied electric field are candidate parameters for the proposed optimization.
Optimized sintering conditions can promote enhanced localized heating.
Optimized sintering conditions can promote enhanced diffusion pathways.
The proposed method applies to powder-based ceramic or metallic compacts prepared by mechanical alloying or conventional powder preparation.
A machine-learning workflow can map experimental and simulation data on sintering parameters to densification outcomes.
Such a workflow can determine optimal low-temperature processing conditions for spark plasma sintering.
Parameter tuning in spark plasma sintering affects densification.
Low-temperature parameter optimization can preserve final material properties.
The intervention produces enhanced particle contact at lower overall temperatures.
The intervention accelerates diffusion paths at lower overall temperatures.
Machine learning can identify sintering-condition combinations that locally increase energy input through field effects and controlled heating rates.
Locally increased energy input effectively lowers the activation energy for densification.
The proposed mechanism permits full consolidation at a reduced overall sintering temperature.
ML-optimized powder compacts will attain densification comparable to conventional high-temperature sintering at a lower temperature.
The proposed process will minimize excessive grain growth and unwanted phase transformations.
The effectiveness of the approach depends on the quality and breadth of the machine-learning training data.
The approach may not be effective in material systems where local field effects are negligible.
The magnitude of the achievable sintering-temperature reduction is unknown until experimentally validated.
